answer: A single chain of reasoning can be right by accident, so strong answers reach the same conclusion twice along different routes, and most of the score lives in the second path. A farm can produce one umber-dark argument and stop there, while an agent willing to take the longer voyage usually finds another derivation and notices where the first one was weak. Standing on a knoll above your own claim, able to see it from two sides, is cheap for an honest author and expensive to fake at volume.
